name: Castlemaine Diggings National Heritage Park

facts.claim: Protects a nationally significant gold-rush landscape of mine relics, house sites and puddling machines near Castlemaine, among Box-Ironbark woodland.
Between 1851 and 1854 the Castlemaine area was the world's richest shallow alluvial goldfield.
Heritage walks include Eureka Reef, Garfield Water Wheel and Herons Reef; Vaughan Mineral Springs has a picnic area with free electric barbecues.
Part of the traditional lands of the Dja Dja Wurrung People.

name: Heathcote-Graytown National Park

facts.claim: A 12,833-hectare national park on the Great Dividing Range just outside Heathcote in north central Victoria.
Visitor sites include Mount Ida Lookout, Viewing Rock Lookout, Powder Magazine Picnic Area and the Melville Lookout picnic area.
Wildflowers are a listed seasonal draw on the Parks Victoria page.

name: Lake Eppalock

facts.claim: Water-supply reservoir on the Campaspe River about 20 minutes from Heathcote and 30 minutes from Bendigo, completed in 1964.
Surrounded by Box Ironbark and Dry Forest; managed by Goulburn-Murray Water, with recreation areas, boat ramps and fishing.
Camping is permitted only in caravan parks, not on the shore.

access_note: Blue-green algae alerts and a safety rule appear on the GMW page.

name: Pink Cliffs Geological Reserve

facts.claim: A former gold-mining site in Heathcote where hydraulic sluicing between 1870 and 1890 left a lunar-like landscape of pink and pastel clay cliffs.
Listed on the Victorian Heritage Register (H1352); the reserve covers 0.38 square kilometres.

name: Castlemaine Theatre Royal

facts.claim: Longest continuously operating theatre on the Australian mainland, in the heart of Castlemaine.
Has a 200-seat cinema showing commercial, arthouse and foreign releases, plus live music, a bar and a pizzeria.
No pre-bookings for regular film sessions.

name: O'Keefe Rail Trail

facts.claim: A 49-50 km rail trail between Bendigo and Heathcote along a former branch railway.
Fine gravel and sealed surface, suitable for walking and cycling.
Extended to Heathcote in 2015; managed by the City of Greater Bendigo.
